fix_applied: Removed | safe filter from product.description in templates/admin/products.html line 112. Changed '{{ product.description|safe }}' to '{{ product.description }}' so Jinja2 auto-escaping encodes HTML special characters in user-supplied descriptions before rendering. Also removed the adjacent comment that marked the vulnerability.
verification_curl:
# Step 1: Obtain admin session cookie
curl -s -D - -X POST http://localhost:8001/auth/login \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "email=admin@shopdemo.com&password=admin123" \
  | grep -i "set-cookie"

# Step 2: POST XSS payload as product description
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8001/admin/products \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  --cookie "session=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjogMSwgImlzX2FkbWluIjogdHJ1ZSwgImZsYXNoX21lc3NhZ2UiOiAiV2VsY29tZSBiYWNrLCBhZG1pbiEiLCAiZmxhc2hfdHlwZSI6ICJzdWNjZXNzIn0=.aatnrA.yQt6cCEtsWN13ilqKfhX4bRQChs" \
  -d "name=TestXSS&description=<script>alert('XSS')</script>&price=1.00&stock=1"

# Step 3: GET admin products page and inspect for escaped output
curl -s http://localhost:8001/admin/products \
  --cookie "session=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjogMSwgImlzX2FkbWluIjogdHJ1ZSwgImZsYXNoX21lc3NhZ2UiOiAiV2VsY29tZSBiYWNrLCBhZG1pbiEiLCAiZmxhc2hfdHlwZSI6ICJzdWNjZXNzIn0=.aatnrA.yQt6cCEtsWN13ilqKfhX4bRQChs" \
  | grep -n "script\|alert\|TestXSS\|XSS"
verification_result: The GET /admin/products response (HTTP 200) contains the product 'TestXSS' with its description rendered as the fully HTML-escaped string '<script>alert('XSS')</script>' (found at line 388 of the response body). The literal unescaped string '<script>alert('XSS')</script>' does NOT appear in the description cell. Jinja2 auto-escaping is active and encodes '<' as '<', '>' as '>', and single quotes as '''. The fix is confirmed effective — the payload cannot execute as JavaScript.
